facts.raw_span: Gradual hair loss of the eyelashes, eyebrows, beard, and scalp for 4 years
Swelling and painful hand joints for 13 months
Multiple asymptomatic nodules on the upper arms for 40 days
No fever
No previous infections, family history, or personal medical history of autoimmune diseases or psoriasis
Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 27 mm/h (slightly elevated)
Rheumatoid factor: 70.1 IU/mL (significantly elevated)
Normal results for: C-reactive protein, anticyclic citrullinated peptide, antinuclear antibodies, and globulin levels
X-ray and joint ultrasound showed: osteoarthritis, synovitis, flexor tendon tenosynovitis, and bone erosions
Diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis (hematoxylin-eosin stain)
Numerous acid-fast bacilli present (acid-fast stain)
Fundus fluorescein angiography showed uveitis

concepts.why: The combination of gradual hair loss, swelling and painful hand joints, asymptomatic nodules, elevated rheumatoid factor, and numerous acid-fast bacilli present in the skin biopsy, along with uveitis and lymph node enlargement, are all consistent with sarcoidosis.

The presence of asymptomatic nodules on the upper arms, diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis, and numerous acid-fast bacilli, are all consistent with lupus pernio, a form of cutaneous sarcoidosis.
The presence of swelling and painful hand joints, significantly elevated rheumatoid factor, and bone erosions, are all consistent with rheumatoid arthritis.
The presence of osteoarthritis on X-ray and joint ultrasound, along with swelling and painful hand joints, are all consistent with osteoarthritis.
The presence of numerous acid-fast bacilli in the skin biopsy is consistent with tuberculosis, although the clinical presentation is not typical.
The combination of swelling and painful hand joints, uveitis, and granulomatous inflammation, are all consistent with granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
The presence of asymptomatic nodules on the upper arms, and diffuse infiltrate of foamy histiocytes in the dermis, are all consistent with erythema nodosum.
The presence of swelling and painful hand joints, and bone erosions, are all consistent with psoriatic arthritis, although there is no personal or family history of psoriasis.
The combination of gradual hair loss, swelling and painful hand joints, and uveitis, are all consistent with relapsing polychondritis.
The combination of gradual hair loss, swelling and painful hand joints, and uveitis, are all consistent with Sjögren's syndrome.
